text:
sam: hi everyone, first day! VPN shows CONNECTED but i can't reach our internal registry at 10.40.9.20. browser gets connection refused. any tips?

lee: welcome! quick check  are you on company laptop or personal? and which VPN client (wireguard/cisco/our-agent)?

sam: company macbook, using our-agent v2.3. client UI says split-tunnel. i ran `netstat -rn` and `scutil --dns` and pasted the bits i think matter below (redacted local IPs):
```
Routing tables:
Destination        Gateway            Flags      Netif Expire
default            192.168.1.1        UGScg      en0
10.40.0.0/16       192.168.1.1        UGSc       en0   <-- hmm
172.31.40.0/24     172.22.100.1       UGSc       utun1

DNS:
resolver #1
  nameserver[0] : 8.8.8.8
resolver #2
  nameserver[0] : 172.22.100.10
```

sam: looks like 10.40/16 is pointing to my router not utun.

lee: yep. two likely causes: (1) client didn't push the route because of home router conflict, or (2) mac prefixed an existing route due to interface metrics. quick workaround: add a route via the vpn interface gw `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 172.22.100.1` then `curl http://10.40.9.20:5000/health`.

sam: how do i find the vpn gw ip? netstat shows utun1 172.22.100.1 per above.

lee: that's the one. try that route add. if it fails with "operation not permitted" you might have to disable System Integrity Protection for that action or use the proper entitlements. but usually route add works.

sam: route add succeeded. curl 10.40.9.20:5000 returned 200 and registry UI loads. thanks! :tada:

arthur: two follow-ups: (1) this won't persist across reboots; for mac we have a simple plist you can drop in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.redwood.addroute.plist to re-add route on login. ping me and i'll send the snippet. (2) i'm filing a ticket to check why our-agent sometimes doesn't push 10.40/16 on macs when local network has a matching net.

infra-bot: Created infra ticket TKT-4558: "split-tunnel route not applied to 10.40/16 on macOS client when LAN overlaps" assigned to @arthur.

sam: sweet. also had an Okta popup during onboarding earlier; okta-bot reminded me to finish SSO in default browser before connecting VPN. fixed that earlier.

lee: pro tip: if you're on flaky home wifi, tether mobile hotspot for first-run onboarding  avoids double-NAT/captive portal issues. added to new-hire checklist.

sam: thanks y'all, saved my morning.
